question: Should OpenClaw guarantee a configurable pre-timeout child warning across runtimes, provide it only for runtimes advertising same-turn steering, or leave hard-timeout recovery as the supported behavior?
rationale: Native child control, generic ACP prompt/cancel, and Codex-specific same-turn steering have different semantics, so code inspection cannot choose the public cross-runtime guarantee or justify a new config surface without maintainer intent.

options.title: Capability-gated warning
options.body: Add a core deadline-warning lifecycle capability and deliver it only through runtimes that explicitly support same-turn input, with documented best-effort behavior elsewhere.

options.title: Native-only warning
options.body: Implement warning delivery for native subagents now and document that ACP runs retain hard-timeout behavior until a portable ACP steer contract exists.

options.title: Keep timeout-only behavior
options.body: Do not add a warning surface and rely on durable progress practices plus post-timeout partial-result and parent-notification improvements.

recommendation.title: Capability-gated warning
recommendation.body: Add a core deadline-warning lifecycle capability and deliver it only through runtimes that explicitly support same-turn input, with documented best-effort behavior elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work covers both native and ACP subagent lifecycle paths, making this the strongest available routing signal for the cross-runtime product choice.
